PUBLIC RESPONSE: 25 and 74

The body of the piece is a double sestina on the six end–words

1 mountains  2 valleys  3 forests  4 music  5 morning  6 evening

Stanza 1 = 1 2 3 4 5 6
Stanza 2 = 6 1 5 2 4 3
Stanza 3 = 3 6 4 1 2 5
Stanza 4 = 5 3 2 6 1 4
Stanza 5 = 4 5 1 3 6 2
Stanza 6 = 2 4 6 5 3 1

and then the six-stanza cycle repeats.  In the text as printed

1-6  1 2 3 4 5 6
7-12 6 1 5 2 4 3
13-18 3 6 4 1 2 5
19-24 5 3 2 6 1 4
25-30 4 5 1 3 6 2
31-36 2 4 6 5 3 1
37-42 1 2 3 4 5 6
43-48 6 1 5 2 4 3
49-54 3 6 4 1 2 5
55-60 5 3 2 6 1 4
61-66 4 5 1 3 6 2
67-72 2 4 6 5 3 1

so the 72 line body is a perfect alternating Strephon / Klaius sestina.

The tornada should be

* L73  mountains in the middle, valleys at the end
* L74  forests in the middle, music at the end
* L75  morning in the middle, evening at the end

L73 = “These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;” and
L75 = “Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.” are correct.

L74 as printed is

74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music

it ends music but contains no forests.  The only line in the whole
poem which ends in music and which also contains forests in the
middle is

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;

It ends music and is the unique forests/music line of the sestina.
Putting 25 back into the tornada and putting the present L74 back into
its place in Stanza 5 restores

L74 forests / music
L25 music

and leaves the end-word sequence of Stanza 5

4 5 1 3 6 2

unchanged, i.e. the normal sestina 4 5 1 3 6 2.  Hence the two
misplaced lines are the present L25 and the present L74.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The six end-words of the double sestina are

1 mountains  2 valleys  3 forests  4 music  5 morning  6 evening

Stanza 1-6 and stanza 7-12 are the two regular sestina sequences

1 2 3 4 5 6
6 1 5 2 4 3
3 6 4 1 2 5
5 3 2 6 1 4
4 5 1 3 6 2
2 4 6 5 3 1

and the tornada is in the usual 1+2 / 3+4 / 5+6 distribution

* 1+2 line ends with b = valleys and contains a = mountains
* 3+4 line ends with d = music and contains c = forests
* 5+6 line ends with f = evening and contains e = morning

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;  → a + b  OK
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.        → e + f  OK

74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music
ends with d = music but it contains no c = forests. The only
music-end line in the whole 72-line body which does contain forests
is

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;

25 ends with music and it is the only music-end line that carries
forests in the body of the line.  25 and 74 are both music-end lines,
so interchanging them leaves the sestina end-word sequence
intact, 25 → music, 74 → music, while restoring the tornada

74 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;
to the required c + d position and putting a neutral music-end
line in the body of the second sestina.

Hence in the printed text the tornada line 74 and the body line 25
have been interchanged.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 25 and 74

The 72-line body is a 12-stanza double sestina on the six terminal
lexemes

1 mountains   2 valleys   3 forests   4 music   5 morning   6 evening

S1 = 1 2 3 4 5 6
K1 = 6 1 5 2 4 3
S2 = 3 6 4 1 2 5
K2 = 5 3 2 6 1 4 ...
and so on, i.e. S1,K1,S2,K2,… is the normal 1 2 3 4 5 6 / 6 1 5 2 4 3 /
3 6 4 1 2 5 / 5 3 2 6 1 4 / 4 5 1 3 6 2 / 2 4 6 5 3 1
rotation repeated. The three-line tornada is meant to be the
classical envoi

* mountains / valleys
* forests / music
* morning / evening

with the six end-words used once each. In the text as printed

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;      – 1/2
74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music                  – 4
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.              – 5/6

the forests end-word is missing from the tornada and the
music line of the tornada has no forests in it.

The only line of the sestina that ends in music and contains forests
in the same line is

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;   – 4

and 25 and 74 both end in music.  Interchanging the two lines keeps
every stanza’s six terminal words intact and restores the tornada to

73 mountains / valleys
74 forests eke, made wretched by our music – forests / music
75 morning / evening

i.e. the regular 1/2 – 3/4 – 5/6 envoi. Hence the misplaced pair is
line 25 with line 74.

with the standard rotation 1 2 3 4 5 6 / 6 1 5 2 4 3 / 3 6 4 1 2 5 / 5 3 2 6 1 4 / 4 5 1 3 6 2 / 2 4 6 5 3 1 repeated for Strephon/Klaius stanzas.

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;

74 These forests eke, made wretched by our music; → forests/music
